source.title: Defining and Characterizing Reward Hacking
source.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35 (NeurIPS 2022)

confidence_rationale: Rigorous formal characterization of WHEN a proxy can diverge from a true objective -- the negative counterpart to Ng et al. High source quality (NeurIPS, formal proofs). Mapping fidelity moderate: the headline impossibility is a worst-case result over ALL stochastic policies, but the paper itself shows non-trivial unhackable proxies exist on RESTRICTED policy sets -- exactly the regime a biological/structured agent occupies, so it both warns and partially reassures. Direction 'mixed' (warns against naive proxy reliance; the escape hatch supports REE's structured-policy setting).
failure_signatures: Over the set of ALL stochastic policies, two reward functions can be unhackable only if one is constant -- a guaranteed-never-divergent non-trivial proxy essentially cannot exist in the unrestricted case.
Assumes a single fixed true reward; for an architecture with multiple homeostatic drives or non-stationary objectives the unhackability comparison must be re-specified per objective.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A proxy reward is 'unhackable' relative to a true reward iff increasing expected proxy return can never decrease expected true return. Over all stochastic policies this is extremely restrictive (only trivial pairs qualify), but non-trivial unhackable pairs DO exist when the policy set is restricted.
mapping.ree_translation: Quantifies the divergence risk that REE's goal-maintenance proxy must avoid, and -- importantly -- shows the risk is governed by the agent's policy manifold. Because REE agents explore a structured, restricted policy space (homeostatic drives, harm constraints, bounded planning), they sit in the regime where non-trivial aligned proxies are POSSIBLE. This makes `proxy_tethering_guard` tractable rather than impossible, and tells the design where to look (restrict/structure the policy set, not just the reward).
mapping.mapping_caveat: Occupancy-measure / expected-return theory over a fixed policy set and a single fixed true reward. REE's multi-drive, non-stationary objective does not match the single-reward assumption, so the formal unhackability statement must be re-derived per drive before it can certify anything in-substrate.
mapping.source_context: RL/AI-safety theory (MDPs, occupancy measures); no empirical agent.

confidence_components.notes: Formal and rigorous; mapping capped by single-reward / full-policy-set assumptions vs REE's multi-drive structured-policy setting. The restricted-policy escape hatch is the most REE-relevant result.
